modules.sub: Am I eligible & how to apply
modules.html:
MODULE 0 · KNOW YOUR NDIS RIGHTS

Getting In

Am I eligible & how do I apply? The front door to the NDIS — who can join, and exactly how to ask.

⏱️ About 11 min 🎯 3 quick activities ✅ Ends with a knowledge check
Scroll to begin — 0% complete
🚀 Start here

Getting onto the NDIS is a process — and it's free

Before you can use your rights, you have to get in. Applying can feel daunting, but it's really just three eligibility questions and one request. There's no cost to apply, and help is available at every step.

This module shows you whether you're likely eligible, exactly how to apply, and what evidence to gather so your application is strong the first time.

The one line to remember: Applying is your right. Getting a "no" isn't the end — you can provide more evidence or ask for a review (that's Module 2).

🎬 Watch: How to apply for access to the NDIS

Official NDIS webinar walking you through the access request from start to finish.

Webinar: How to apply for access to the NDIS
Tap play to watch here
Open on YouTube ↗
✅ Activity 1 · Am I eligible?

The 3 questions the NDIS asks

To join, you need to meet all three: age, residence, and either the disability or early intervention test. Tap each to see what it means.

This is a guide, not a decision. Only the NDIS can decide eligibility. If you're unsure, apply anyway or call 1800 800 110 — you don't have to work it out alone.
📝 Activity 2 · How to apply

Making an access request, step by step

Applying is called making an access request. Tap each step to see what to do.

Fastest way to start: call the NDIS on 1800 800 110 and say you'd like to make a verbal access request. They'll walk you through it.
📄 Activity 3 · What evidence do I need?

What makes an application strong

Good evidence is what gets you approved. Tap each to see what to gather.

Tip: Ask your GP, specialist, OT or psychologist to describe how your disability affects your everyday life — not just the diagnosis. Impact is what matters most.
💥 Myth-buster

True or false? Tap to bust the myth

Tap each to reveal the truth.

🧠 Knowledge check

What would you do?

Pick an answer and you'll see straight away why it's right.

📞 Keep this handy

Help to apply

1800 800 110
Make a verbal access request. Mon–Fri.
Free advocate
1800 643 787
Help to apply and gather evidence.
Your GP / treating team
Your clinic
They provide the disability evidence you need.
Interpreter (TIS)
131 450
Free interpreting for your application.
Got in? Next stop is your first plan — head to Module 1: Your Rights and you'll be ready. Said no? Module 2 shows you how to ask for a review.
🎉 You did it

Module 0 recap

  • ✔ You need age (0–64 when you apply), residence, and the disability OR early intervention test.
  • ✔ Apply by making an access request — call 1800 800 110 or fill in the form.
  • ✔ Prove your identity/residence and give disability evidence from your treating professionals.
  • ✔ The NDIS aims to decide within 21 days of having all your information.
  • ✔ A "no" isn't final — add evidence or ask for a review (Module 2). Applying is free.
Educational content for people considering the NDIS. Based on the NDIS "Eligibility requirements" and "Access Request Form" guidance. This is general information, not an eligibility decision — only the NDIS can decide. Always check ndis.gov.au for the latest.

modules.title: Your Rights
modules.html:
MODULE 1 · KNOW YOUR NDIS RIGHTS

Your Rights, Your NDIS

The NDIS is your plan. This module shows you the rights you already have — in plain English.

⏱️ About 12 min 🎯 5 quick activities ✅ Ends with a knowledge check
Scroll to begin — 0% complete
🚀 Start here

Why your rights matter

You don't have to be an expert to get the NDIS right. But knowing your rights changes everything — it helps you speak up, ask questions, and get the support you're meant to get.

The NDIS runs on one big idea: choice and control. That means you decide how you live your life and how your supports work — not someone deciding for you. These rights come from Australian law (the NDIS Act) and an international agreement Australia signed: the UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities.

The one line to remember: You are the expert in your own life. Everyone in the NDIS is meant to work with you, not over you.

🎬 Watch: You choose it, you control it

A quick video on what choice and control really means for your NDIS plan.

NDIS Plan: You Choose It, You Control It
Tap play to watch here
Open on YouTube ↗
🃏 Activity 1 · Tap to flip

Your 5 promises from the NDIS

The NDIS made a written promise to every participant, called the Participant Service Charter. It's 5 things they must always do. Tap each card to see what it means for you.

💡 These aren't "nice to haves" — they're the standard you can hold the NDIS to.

🎬 Watch: Respecting your rights

A short video on what it looks like when your rights are genuinely respected.

Respecting your Rights!
Tap play to watch here
Open on YouTube ↗
⏰ Activity 2 · The NDIS has deadlines

How long should things take?

Most people don't know this: the NDIS gives itself legal time limits to do things. It's called the Participant Service Guarantee. If they're slow, you have the right to ask why. Tap a task to see the deadline.

21days (or fewer)
Decide if you can access the NDIS — after they have all your information.
Tip: These are maximum times. Write down the date you asked for something. If the deadline passes, that's your cue to follow up or make a complaint.
🛡️ Activity 3 · Your safety shield

What every worker & provider MUST do

Anyone paid to support you must follow the NDIS Code of Conduct. Think of it as a shield around you. These are the 7 rules they can never break:

    🎬 Watch: Your right to privacy

    A short video on what the Code of Conduct means when it comes to keeping your information private.

    NDIS Code of Conduct: Privacy
    Tap play to watch here
    Open on YouTube ↗
    If someone breaks these rules, you can report them — free and confidential — to the NDIS Quality and Safeguards Commission on 1800 035 544. You can complain about anyone, even if they aren't a "registered" provider.
    💥 Activity 4 · Myth-buster

    True or false? Tap to bust the myth

    Lots of "rules" people believe about the NDIS are simply wrong. Tap each one to reveal the truth.

    🧠 Knowledge check

    What would you do?

    No pressure — this is just to help it stick. Pick an answer and you'll see straight away why it's right.

    📞 Keep this handy

    Where to get help

    NDIS (general)
    1800 800 110
    Plans, payments, questions. Mon–Fri.
    Quality & Safeguards Commission
    1800 035 544
    To report a worker or provider. Free & confidential.
    Free NDIS advocate
    1800 643 787
    Disability Advocacy Finder — someone on your side.
    Interpreter (TIS)
    131 450
    Free translating & interpreting in your language.
    Coming up: The NDIS is changing. New "flexible budgets" and a new needs-assessment conversation start rolling out from 2027 — we'll cover what that means for your rights in a later module.
    🎉 You did it

    Module 1 recap

    • ✔ The NDIS runs on choice and control — you're the expert in your own life.
    • ✔ The NDIS made you 5 promises: transparent, responsive, respectful, empowering, connected.
    • ✔ There are legal deadlines (the Service Guarantee) you can hold them to.
    • ✔ A 7-rule Code of Conduct protects you — and you can report breaches on 1800 035 544.
    • ✔ You can get a free advocate to stand beside you any time.
    Educational content for NDIS participants. Rights and timeframes are based on the NDIS Participant Service Charter, Participant Service Guarantee, and the NDIS Code of Conduct (NDIS Quality and Safeguards Commission). Always check ndis.gov.au for the latest.

modules.title: Speaking Up
modules.html:
MODULE 2 · KNOW YOUR NDIS RIGHTS

Speaking Up

Complaints, reviews & getting help — how to actually use the rights from Module 1 when something's not right.

⏱️ About 12 min 🎯 5 quick activities ✅ Ends with a knowledge check
Scroll to begin — 0% complete
🚀 Start here

Speaking up is your right — not being "difficult"

In Module 1 you learned the rights you have. This module is about what to do when those rights aren't being met — when a service is poor, a worker crosses a line, or the NDIS makes a decision you don't agree with.

Here's the mindset shift: complaining is not rude, and it won't get you in trouble. It's how the whole system stays safe and fair. Every person you deal with is meant to make it easy for you to raise concerns.

The one line to remember: If something feels wrong, you're allowed to say so — and there's always someone whose job is to help you.

🎬 Watch: The Participant Service Charter & Improvement Plan

A quick how-to on the promises the NDIS makes to you — and the plan for making its service better.

NDIS Participant Service Charter & Improvement Plan
Tap play to watch here
Open on YouTube ↗
🚪 Activity 1 · Where do I go?

The 3 doors for a problem

Not every problem goes to the same place. Here's the simple map of who handles what.

🧑‍🔧

Problem with a service or worker

Bad support, feeling unsafe, being treated badly.
→ Provider, then the Commission
📄

Unhappy with an NDIS decision

Plan, funding, or eligibility decision you disagree with.
→ Ask for a review
🤝

Need someone on your side

You want help to speak up or understand your options.
→ Free advocate
Not sure which door? That's okay. Call the free advocacy line on 1800 643 787 or the NDIS on 1800 800 110 and just describe what happened — they'll point you the right way.
📣 Activity 2 · Making a complaint

How to complain about a provider or worker

Tap each step to see what happens. You can stop at any step if the problem gets fixed.

Report a worker or provider: NDIS Quality and Safeguards Commission — 1800 035 544 or online at ndiscommission.gov.au. It's free, and you can ask to stay anonymous.
⚖️ Activity 3 · Disagree with a decision?

The review ladder

If the NDIS makes a decision you don't agree with — about your plan, funding or access — you don't just have to accept it. You climb the ladder, one rung at a time. Watch the deadlines.

1️⃣

Ask for an internal review

A different NDIS staff member looks at the decision again. This is free and it's your first step.

⏰ You have 3 months from the decision to ask
↓ still not happy?
2️⃣

Go to the Administrative Review Tribunal (ART)

An independent body (it replaced the AAT in October 2024) reviews the decision. Free support is available through the NDIS Appeals Program.

⏰ Apply within 28 days of the internal review result
You don't have to do this alone. A free advocate can help you request a review and even support you at the Tribunal. Find one on 1800 643 787. Tip: you can't use your NDIS funds to pay a lawyer for the Tribunal, but the free Appeals support is there for exactly this.
💥 Activity 4 · Myth-buster

True or false? Tap to bust the myth

Fear of speaking up usually comes from myths. Tap each to reveal the truth.

🧠 Knowledge check

What would you do?

Pick an answer and you'll see straight away why it's right.

📞 Keep this handy

Who to call

Complaints about a provider/worker
1800 035 544
NDIS Quality & Safeguards Commission. Free, can be anonymous.
Reviews & general NDIS
1800 800 110
Ask for an internal review of a decision. Mon–Fri.
Free advocate (on your side)
1800 643 787
Disability Advocacy Finder — help to speak up & appeal.
Interpreter (TIS)
131 450
Free interpreting in your language, any of the above calls.
In immediate danger? Always call 000 first. The complaints process is for after everyone is safe.
🎉 You did it

Module 2 recap

  • ✔ Speaking up is your right — it's free and it won't cost you your funding.
  • ✔ 3 doors: service problems → provider then the Commission; decision problems → a review; need backup → an advocate.
  • ✔ Complaints about workers/providers go to the Commission on 1800 035 544 (can be anonymous).
  • ✔ Disagree with a decision? Internal review within 3 months, then the ART within 28 days.
  • ✔ A free advocate (1800 643 787) can stand beside you the whole way.
Educational content for NDIS participants. Based on the NDIS "Guide to decision reviews", the NDIS Quality and Safeguards Commission complaints process, and the Participant Service Guarantee. The Administrative Review Tribunal replaced the AAT on 14 October 2024. Always check ndis.gov.au and ndiscommission.gov.au for the latest.

modules.title: Your Plan
modules.html:
MODULE 3 · KNOW YOUR NDIS RIGHTS

Your NDIS Plan

Reading it & spending it with confidence — what the money is, where it sits, and what you can actually use it on.

⏱️ About 13 min 🎯 5 quick activities ✅ Ends with a knowledge check
Scroll to begin — 0% complete
🚀 Start here

Your plan is your toolkit — not a mystery

Your NDIS plan is really two things: your goals, and the funding to help you reach them. A lot of stress comes from not knowing what the money is for or how to use it. Let's fix that.

The golden rule for spending: a support must be "reasonable and necessary" — meaning it relates to your disability, helps you pursue your goals, is good value, and isn't just a normal living cost everyone has (like rent or groceries).

The one line to remember: It's your money to reach your goals. If you understand your 3 budgets and who holds them, you're in control.

🎬 Watch: NDIS overview — how it all works

A big-picture refresher on how the NDIS works, who's eligible, and how funding and support options fit together.

NDIS Overview: How It All Works
Tap play to watch here
Open on YouTube ↗
💰 Activity 1 · Your 3 pots of money

Where your funding sits

Your plan splits funding into 3 budgets. They work differently — some are flexible, some are locked. Tap each to see what it covers.

Why flexibility matters: Core is the budget you can move around most freely. Capacity Building and Capital are usually locked to what they were approved for — so plan those carefully.
🗝️ Activity 2 · Who holds the money?

3 ways to manage your plan

You get to choose how your funding is handled. This changes how much control you have — and which providers you can use.

Good to know: You can mix these across budgets, and you can ask to change how your plan is managed. Plan management fees don't come out of your other supports — they're funded separately.
✅ Activity 3 · Would the NDIS fund it?

Reasonable & necessary — yes or no?

Tap each item to see if the NDIS would usually fund it, and why. This is the "reasonable and necessary" test in action.

Not sure about an item? Ask before you buy. Check with your plan manager, support coordinator, or the NDIS on 1800 800 110. Keep receipts for anything you spend.

A short explainer on the test the NDIS uses to decide what it will fund.

What is "Reasonable and Necessary"?

Open on YouTube ↗

Heads up — change coming: From 2027 the NDIS begins moving to new "flexible budgets" and a needs-assessment conversation. The 3 budgets you learned here still apply now; we'll cover the new system when it lands.
🎉 You did it

Module 3 recap

  • ✔ Your plan = your goals + the funding to reach them.
  • ✔ 3 budgets: Core (flexible daily supports), Capacity Building (building skills), Capital (equipment & modifications).
  • ✔ 3 ways to manage it: self-managed (most control), plan-managed (a manager pays), or NDIA-managed (registered providers only).
  • ✔ Spend on reasonable & necessary disability supports — not everyday costs everyone has.
  • ✔ Unsure? Ask first, keep receipts — and a free advocate can help.
Educational content for NDIS participants. Based on NDIS guidance on managing your plan, budget categories (Core, Capacity Building, Capital), and the "reasonable and necessary" criteria. Rules are changing from 2027. Always check ndis.gov.au for the latest and confirm specific purchases with the NDIS or your plan manager.

modules.title: Managing Providers
modules.html:
MODULE 4 · KNOW YOUR NDIS RIGHTS

Choosing & Managing Providers

Getting great support — and confidently ditching support that isn't working. You're the boss; they work for you.

⏱️ About 14 min 🎯 5 quick activities ✅ Ends with a knowledge check
Scroll to begin — 0% complete
🚀 Start here

You're hiring — so you get to choose

Providers and support workers are the people you actually spend your funding on. Here's the mindset: they work for you. You can shop around, ask questions, say no, and switch if it's not right — just like hiring anyone else.

Choice and control (from Module 1) is real here. You don't have to take the first provider offered, stay with one you don't like, or accept poor service because you feel awkward.

The one line to remember: A good provider earns your trust and makes it easy to leave. A dodgy one pressures you and makes it hard.

🎬 Watch: What is a service agreement?

Short official explainer on what a service agreement is and why it protects you.

How To — What is a service agreement?
Tap play to watch here
Open on YouTube ↗
❓ Activity 1 · Before you hire

5 questions to ask any provider

Before you sign up with anyone, ask these. Tap each to see why it matters.

Where to find providers: the NDIS Provider Finder (in the myplace portal or at ndis.gov.au), your support coordinator, or word of mouth from other participants. It's fine to talk to a few before choosing.
🏷️ Activity 2 · Registered or not?

Registered vs unregistered providers

Both must follow the Code of Conduct and have a complaints process. The difference is oversight — and which one you can use depends on how your plan is managed.

✅ Registered

  • ＋ Audited & checked by the NDIS Commission
  • ＋ Must meet the NDIS Practice Standards
  • ＋ Needed for some supports (e.g. SDA, plan management)
  • － Can cost more; sometimes less flexible

🔓 Unregistered

  • ＋ Often smaller, flexible, sometimes cheaper
  • ＋ Still must follow the Code of Conduct
  • － Less regular oversight from the Commission
  • － Can't provide some supports (e.g. SDA)
How your plan is managed
Can you use unregistered?
🙋 Self-managed
✅ Yes
🧾 Plan-managed
✅ Yes
🏢 NDIA-managed
❌ Registered only
📄 Activity 3 · Service agreement decoder

What's in a service agreement?

A service agreement is your contract with a provider — it protects you. It's not always legally required, but it's smart to have one. Tap each part to know what to check before you sign.

Golden rule: Never feel rushed to sign. Take it home, read it, ask questions, get help from an advocate or plan manager. A good provider is happy to wait.
🚩 Activity 4 · Spot the red flag

Red flag or all good?

Tap each situation to see if it's a warning sign — and what to do about it.

Spotted a red flag? You can leave (check your agreement's notice period, or leave immediately if you're unsafe) and report the provider to the NDIS Commission on 1800 035 544.
💥 Activity 5 · Myth-buster

True or false? Tap to bust the myth

Tap each to reveal the truth.

🧠 Knowledge check

Pick an answer and you'll see straight away why it's right.

📞 Keep this handy

Provider help & safety

1800 800 110
Provider Finder & general questions. Mon–Fri.
Report a provider/worker
1800 035 544
NDIS Quality & Safeguards Commission. Free, can be anonymous.
Free advocate

Help to choose, question, or leave a provider.
Interpreter (TIS)

Free interpreting in your language.
In immediate danger? Call 000 first — always.
🎉 You did it

Module 4 recap

  • ✔ Providers work for you — shop around, ask questions, and don't feel rushed.
  • ✔ Registered = more oversight; unregistered = often flexible. Both follow the Code of Conduct.
  • ✔ A service agreement protects you — check the services, costs, cancellation and notice period before signing.
  • ✔ Watch for red flags: pressure, vague agreements, blank forms, charging for no-shows.
  • ✔ You can switch providers — check your notice period, leave immediately if unsafe, and report bad ones on 1800 035 544.
Educational content for NDIS participants. Based on NDIS guidance on working with providers, service agreements, and the difference between registered and unregistered providers under the NDIS Quality and Safeguards Commission. Always check ndis.gov.au and ndiscommission.gov.au for the latest.

modules.title: Staying Safe
modules.html:
MODULE 5 · KNOW YOUR NDIS RIGHTS

Staying Safe

Your right to be free from abuse, neglect & exploitation — how to spot it, and exactly who to tell.

⏱️ About 12 min 🎯 4 quick activities ✅ Ends with a knowledge check
💛 Need help right now?
🚨 Emergency: 000 ☎️ Abuse & Neglect Hotline: 1800 880 052 🛡️ NDIS Commission: 1800 035 544
Scroll to begin — 0% complete
🚀 Start here

You have the right to feel safe — always

Being safe is not a bonus. It's a right. You have the right to be treated well, to feel safe in your home and with the people who support you, and to be free from anyone who hurts, frightens, controls, or takes advantage of you.

This module can bring up hard feelings — take it at your own pace, and skip ahead or take a break if you need to. The most important message is simple:

If someone is hurting you, it is not your fault — and it is never "just how it is." You are allowed to tell someone, and people will help.
💛 This module mentions abuse and neglect. If it feels like too much, that's okay — you can stop, talk to someone you trust, or call the Abuse & Neglect Hotline on 1800 880 052.

🎬 Watch: NDIS Code of Conduct — Safety & Competency

Short official NDIS Commission video on what safe and competent support looks like.

NDIS Code of Conduct: Safety & Competency
Tap play to watch here
Open on YouTube ↗
🔎 Activity 1 · Know the types

Harm can look like different things

Abuse isn't only about being hit. It comes in different forms — and all of them are wrong. Tap each to understand it in plain words.

Remember: You don't need proof or a perfect explanation to speak up. If something doesn't feel right, that's enough of a reason to tell someone.
⚠️ Activity 2 · Warning signs

Signs something might be wrong

These can be signs that you — or someone you know — is being harmed. One sign alone doesn't prove anything, but it's a reason to check in.

Worried about a friend? You can report abuse of someone else too. Trust your gut and make the call — the hotline (1800 880 052) will help you work out what to do.
📣 Activity 3 · Who to tell

Speaking up — who does what

You can tell a person you trust first — family, a friend, an advocate. When you're ready to report, here's who to call and what they do.

Good to know: Support workers must have an NDIS Worker Screening Check, and providers must report serious incidents to the Commission. You're allowed to ask a worker if they've been screened.
⛓️ Know your right

Being restrained or restricted

Sometimes a provider might try to control your behaviour — like locking a door, holding you, or giving medication to calm you. These are called restrictive practices, and you have the right to be free from ones that aren't properly authorised.

They are only ever allowed as a last resort, must be formally approved, written into a plan, and reported. If this is happening to you and you didn't agree to it, that's something to raise with the NDIS Commission on 1800 035 544.

💥 Activity 4 · Myth-buster

True or false? Tap to bust the myth

Fear and shame keep people silent. Let's clear up the myths that stop people getting help.

🧠 Knowledge check

What would you do?

Pick an answer and you'll see straight away why it's right. There's no wrong way to ask for help.

📞 Keep this handy

Your safety contacts

Emergency (danger now)
000
Police, fire, ambulance. Text 106 if you can't speak/hear.
Abuse & Neglect Hotline
1800 880 052
Free, confidential, understands disability. Mon–Fri.
NDIS Commission
1800 035 544
Report a worker or provider. Free, can be anonymous.
Free advocate
1800 643 787
Someone on your side to help you speak up.
National Relay Service
1800 555 677
Then ask for the number you need. For speech/hearing.
Interpreter (TIS)
13 14 50
Free interpreting in your language.
🎉 You did it

Module 5 recap

  • ✔ You have the right to be safe — abuse is never your fault.
  • ✔ Harm has many forms: physical, sexual, emotional, financial, neglect, and unauthorised restraint.
  • ✔ Trust the warning signs — you don't need proof to speak up.
  • ✔ You can tell someone you trust, or call: 000, the Hotline 1800 880 052, or the Commission 1800 035 544.
  • ✔ A free advocate (1800 643 787) can help you every step of the way.
You made it through a hard topic. That takes courage. Knowing this keeps you — and the people you care about — safer.
Educational content for NDIS participants. Based on guidance from the NDIS Quality and Safeguards Commission and the National Disability Abuse and Neglect Hotline. If you are in immediate danger, always call 000. Always check ndiscommission.gov.au for the latest.

modules.title: Your Plan Review
modules.html:
MODULE 6 · KNOW YOUR NDIS RIGHTS

Your Plan Review

Getting ready & getting what you need — walk into your reassessment prepared, and walk out with the right plan.

⏱️ About 13 min 🎯 4 quick activities ✅ Ends with a knowledge check
Scroll to begin — 0% complete
🚀 Start here

Your plan doesn't last forever — and that's a good thing

Every so often the NDIS looks at your plan again to make sure it still fits your life. This is your chance to fix what isn't working and ask for what you need. The secret? People who prepare get better plans.

You've done the hard work in Modules 1–5: you know your rights, how to speak up, your budgets, your providers, and how to stay safe. This module puts it all together for the moment it matters most — your plan review.

The one line to remember: A reassessment isn't a test you can fail. It's a conversation about your life — and you can prepare for it.

🎬 Watch: How To — Your NDIS Plan Review

Short official explainer on what happens at a plan review and how to prepare.

How To — Your NDIS Plan Review
Tap play to watch here
Open on YouTube ↗
🗂️ Activity 1 · Decode the words

Check-in, reassessment, variation?

The NDIS uses three words that sound similar but mean different things. Tap each to understand it in plain English.

📋 Activity 2 · Your prep checklist

What to think about & bring

Good preparation is the difference between an okay plan and a great one. Tap each item to see why it matters.

The most powerful thing to bring: reports from your therapists, doctor or support workers that show how your supports help you — and what you'll need next. Evidence wins plans.
🎯 Activity 3 · Make your goals strong

Weak goal → strong goal

Your goals shape your funding. Vague goals get vague plans. Tap each to see how to turn a weak goal into a strong one.

Strong goals are: specific, connected to your disability, and clear about the support you'd need to get there.
🗓️ Activity 4 · What to expect

How a plan review unfolds

Knowing the steps takes away the stress. Tap each stage to see what happens.

Don't panic about timing: if your reassessment isn't finished by the time your plan ends, your current plan usually keeps going (up to 12 months) so your supports don't stop.
💥 Myth-buster

True or false? Tap to bust the myth

Tap each to reveal the truth.

🧠 Knowledge check

What would you do?

Pick an answer and you'll see straight away why it's right.

📞 Keep this handy

Help to prepare

NDIS (reviews & questions)
1800 800 110
Ask about your check-in or reassessment date. Mon–Fri.
Support coordinator / plan manager
In your plan
Can help you prepare and gather evidence.
Free advocate
1800 643 787
Can sit with you in the meeting and speak up for you.
Interpreter (TIS)
131 450
Free interpreting for your meeting.
Didn't get the plan you needed? You can ask for an internal review within 3 months — that's Module 2. Your rights don't stop at the meeting.
🎉 You did it

Module 6 recap

  • ✔ A reassessment is a fresh plan — a chance to fix what's not working.
  • ✔ A check-in comes first (2–3 months before); a variation is a smaller change.
  • ✔ Prepare: goals, what's working / not, life changes, and evidence from professionals.
  • ✔ Strong goals = specific, disability-related, clear about the support you need.
  • ✔ You can bring an advocate, request a change anytime, and appeal if you disagree.
That's the full course. You now know your rights, how to speak up, your plan and money, your providers, staying safe, and how to get the plan you need. That's real power. 💜
Educational content for NDIS participants. Based on the NDIS guidance "What is a plan reassessment" and "How to prepare for a plan reassessment". Timeframes come from the Participant Service Guarantee. Rules are changing from 2027. Always check ndis.gov.au for the latest.

modules.title: Your Decisions
modules.html:
MODULE 7 · KNOW YOUR NDIS RIGHTS

Making Your Own Decisions

Your voice, supported decision-making & nominees — how to stay in charge of your own life, with the right help.

⏱️ About 12 min 🎯 4 quick activities ✅ Ends with a knowledge check
Scroll to begin — 0% complete
🚀 Start here

Your life, your call

Having a disability doesn't mean other people decide for you. The starting point is always the same: you make your own decisions — and if you need help to do that, you get the help, not have the decision taken away.

This is called supported decision-making, and it's a core NDIS value that flows straight from "choice and control" in Module 1. This module shows you the people who can help — and makes sure you know where the power really sits: with you.

The one line to remember: Getting help to decide is not the same as losing control. With the right support, the decision stays yours.

🎬 Watch: Let's talk supported decision-making

Webinar on what supported decision-making really means and how it works in the NDIS.

Webinar: Let's talk supported decision-making
Tap play to watch here
Open on YouTube ↗
⚖️ Activity 1 · The big idea

Two ways decisions get made

There are two very different approaches. The NDIS wants the first one wherever possible.

🤝

Supported decision-making

Someone helps you decide — they explain the options and what might happen. You stay in charge and make the final call.

✅ The goal — used first
🧑‍⚖️

Substitute decision-making

Someone else makes the decision for you. This is only used when you can't be supported to make it yourself.

⚠️ Last resort only
Why it matters: Even when someone helps or decides for you, they must find out what you want, act in your interests, and help you build your own confidence to decide.
👥 Activity 2 · Who's who

The people who can help you decide

Different helpers have different amounts of power. The purple dots show how much decision-making they take on. Tap each to learn more.

Notice the pattern: most of these help you decide. Only a plan nominee or guardian actually decides for you — and only when you can't or don't want to decide yourself.
🙋 Activity 3 · Whose decision is it?

Spoiler: usually yours

Tap each one to see who really gets to decide. You might be surprised how much is yours.

🎉 You did it

Module 7 recap

  • ✔ The starting point is always: you decide, with support if you need it.
  • ✔ Supported decision-making (help to decide) comes first; substitute (deciding for you) is a last resort.
  • ✔ A correspondence nominee gets your info; a plan nominee makes NDIS plan decisions — only if you can't or don't want to.
  • ✔ A guardian is different — appointed by a tribunal for broader life decisions, as a last resort.
  • ✔ Any nominee must act on your wishes, and you can change or cancel the arrangement.
Educational content for NDIS participants. Based on NDIS guidance "What is a nominee" and the Office of the Public Advocate's guide to NDIS decision-making. Guardianship laws differ by state and territory. Always check ndis.gov.au and your state's Public Advocate/Guardian for the latest.

🅴🆁 EASY READ VERSION

Know your NDIS rights

A short, easy version of the course.
Big words are made small.

⚖️ Your rights

💪

The NDIS is your plan.
You are in charge.

🗣️

You choose how you live your life.
This is called choice and control.

🤝

People must treat you with respect.
They must listen to you.

👂

You can ask for information you understand.
You can use an interpreter for free.

📣 Speaking up

✅

If something is wrong, you can tell someone.
You will not get in trouble.

🧑‍🔧

Problem with a worker or service?
Talk to the provider first.

📞

Still a problem?
Call the NDIS Commission on 1800 035 544.

📄

Don’t agree with an NDIS decision?
You can ask them to look at it again.
You have 3 months to ask.

💰 Your plan and money

🎯

Your plan has your goals.
And money to help you reach them.

🧺

Your money is in 3 pots:
Core, Capacity Building, Capital.

💳

The money is for supports for your disability.
Not for everyday things like food or rent.

❓

Not sure if you can buy something?
Ask first.
Keep the receipt.

🤝 Your workers & providers

👷

Providers work for you.
You can choose them.
You can change them.

📝

Sign a service agreement before you start.
Read it slowly.
Take it home first.

🚩

Never sign a blank form.
Never let someone rush you.
These are warning signs.

🛡️ Staying safe

💛

You have the right to feel safe.
Every day.

🛑

Nobody is allowed to hurt you.
Nobody is allowed to scare you.
Nobody is allowed to take your money.

💔

If someone hurts you, it is not your fault.

📢

You can tell someone you trust.
You can call for help.

🙋 Your decisions

🧠

You make your own decisions.
People can help you decide.

🤝

Getting help to decide is not the same as losing control.
The choice is still yours.
